newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up again, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up again, more gains seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped more than five percent on Friday, extending a 14-day bull run, and traders said continuing foreign demand could spark further price rises.
The seven share SBI index rose 65.56 points or 5.31 percent to 1,299.70. The index has climbed 18.5 percent since the start of the week.
Turnover reached 1.1 billion tolars, up from 799.1 million on Thursday.

"Foreigners are buying at prices that were unimaginable before," said Karmen Cerar at brokerage Potreza. She saw additional uncovered foreign demand which could boost the SBI index in the coming week.
Overall six shares rose, 11 fell and seven were untraded.
Turnover in SKB was brisk at 607.6 million tolars on rumours the bank may list its shares in London.
Pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus was the biggest gainer, firming 9.36 percent to 16,130 tolars on volume of 1,260 shares for total turnover of 20.3 million tolars.
Financial consultancies Primofin and Dadas were the leading decliners, falling by 10 percent apiece. Dadas closed at 21,780 tolars on volume of 252 shares for total turnover of 5.5 million tolars.
Primofin ended at 22,230 tolars on volume of 65 shares for total turnover of 1.4 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
